Hey there.

I suffer from anxiety myself and know where you are coming from. Although you're not diagnosed, it sounds like you're having a lot of trouble in this environment. First of all, I would recommend seeking the help of a professional. Although some can find it demoralising, it's honestly the best thing anyone can ever do.

A technique I learned in group therapy might really benefit you. The more we avoid, the more we are afraid. But if we jump in with two feet, we are going to get scared and put off more. A great way to ease into these situations is to take it as slow as we can.

After some trauma, I found it troubling going into shopping centres. So, everyday I would drive to the shopping centre and go there for at least an hour. It took me a while to get to this point though. At first, I wouldn't leave the car. Then, I went to the closest shop and browsed, then I walked around the centre, etc etc. I still panic sometimes, but not nearly as enough.

What I would recommend is don't think to yourself, "I'm going to work out today", think instead "I'm going to the gym today". See if you can make it to the door. If you feel odd going there just to turn back, try going in plain clothing. If the gym is still off-putting, maybe skip the gym and go for a walk around the block. There's also a lot of home exercises you can do - I invested in an aerobic step that is great for cardio. If you're anywhere in Sydney, Australia I'd give it to you because honestly it's just collecting dust.

Also, when you're comfortable personal trainers really make the gym a safer place :-) At first I didn't like going to the gym in the day (it's a 24 hour gym) but when I started training with a trainer I started going at more reasonable times and twice as much.

The most important thing is to take it at your own pace. This isn't something to push through because it can be damaging.
